modules.name: Layer 0 project schema
modules.design_question: Which one JSON document lets Vista, Form Studio, PVV and the toolbench exchange site, context, massing, floors and programme mix without re-typing, and compare heights with cone ceilings?
modules.method: Floors: PVV's record (level, elevation_m, height_m, area_m2, area_basis, mix of programme_id and share) plus tower_id, unique on (tower_id, level). PVV's normaliseFloors rejects repeated levels and rebuilds each floor from fixed keys, so its adapter filters one tower or aggregates per level, records the choice in provenance, and keeps foreign fields host-side or in ext.pvv. Sites are lon/lat in the City's NAD83(CSRS) as served (M03). Every height-bearing object (Massing, ViewStudy, ContextRef, ceiling) carries vertical{datum, grade_z_m, grade_source}; an absolute-height comparison returns unknown unless both datums match and neither is model_relative. Context layers are references (manifest URL, SHA-256, licence, attribution), never geometry copies. Every estimate carries a basis: measured, derived, assumed or unknown. Tool state lives under ext.<tool>. Reserve top-level floors, settings and brief: PVV's importer reads them (app.js line 841). Validate with JSON Schema 2020-12 through Ajv, then a custom validator for rules a schema cannot state: floor contiguity 0.01 m, share sums 1e-6, level numbering, area_basis enum, datum agreement. Write export adapters first. Offer CityJSON 2.0.1 LoD1 export, not as the working format.
inputs: Vista example study media/example-study.json (25,508 B) as the first fixture.
Form Studio design JSON and .3dm; PVV project JSON and CSV template; DT Mass prisms (x, y, w, d, z0, floors, f2f) with consent.
City parcel and view-cone records; council-published cone ceilings (M03); competition brief constants (79.2 x 144.8 m site, 9.0 FSR non-residential, 244 to 305 m).
City 2009 footprints and 2022 LiDAR for grade_z and measured roof heights (M06).
outputs: layer0.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12), one $id per port type: Frame, Site, ContextRef, Placement, Massing, Floors, Program, ViewStudy, Checks.
Four example files: Library Square site, Shangri-La replacement (from Vista's example), five-floor PVV template, two-tower fixture.
toLayer0 and fromLayer0 adapters per tool; custom validator; CityJSON LoD1 exporter.

modules.name: Shared frame, CRS and vertical datum
modules.design_question: Which horizontal frame, horizontal datum and vertical datum should every tool share, so a point or a height in one tool lands on the same ground, and cone ceiling, in another?
modules.method: Frames in use. legacy-vista-1 (Vista, Form Studio, PVV): x=(lon+123.1207)*111,320*cos(49.2827 deg), y=(lat-49.2827)*110,574. legacy-dtmass-1 (DT Mass): origin (-123.118, 49.283), scales 72,616.63 and 110,574; its origin lies 196.07 m east and 33.17 m north of Vista's. 110,574 m is the equatorial degree of latitude; at 49.28 N it is 111,215 m, so N-S is 0.58% short, E-W 0.19% short, areas 0.77% small. Recommendation: master positions as lon/lat in the City's NAD83(CSRS) as served; a portal parcel corner matches the council's UTM 10N values to 0.11 m. Working frame vtm-local-1: transverse Mercator, lat_0 49.2827, lon_0 -123.1207, k=1, GRS80. Exchange frame EPSG:3157, whose grid areas are 0.080% small, so unfit for FSR. Keep named converters for both legacy frames. Vertical: declare datum and grade_z everywhere. City LiDAR is CGVD28 (Metro Vancouver geoid); NRCan says CGVD28 and CGVD2013 differ enough to matter at LiDAR accuracy; convert only with NRCan GPS-H, never a typed offset. WGS 84 or GNSS inputs differ from NAD83(CSRS) by about 2 m: transform with NRCan parameters and log it.

modules.name: Nodes with typed ports: minimal refactor
modules.design_question: What is the smallest change that lets each tool read and write Layer 0 through typed ports without a rewrite?
modules.method: Each tool gets one manifest (vtm-node.json: id, version, author, licence, entry URL, origin, input and output port types, transports) and two functions: read(layer0) and write() returning a patch of the subtrees it owns. A port is a JSON Pointer typed by schema $id (Site, Placement, Massing, Floors, Program, Checks, ViewStudy); the host validates with Ajv and the custom validator before delivery. Transport 1, no code: file export and import. Transport 2: same-origin storage plus BroadcastChannel among Ruijie's tools on ruijieliu6.github.io (storage keys are namespaced). Transport 3: window.postMessage with an exact targetOrigin and an event.origin check, for classmates, only after written consent. Pages sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, so packs load cross-origin. PVV adapter: read floors for one tower_id or aggregate per level, write floors unchanged, replace window.claude with host services. Order: PVV, Form Studio export, then Vista, the shell and classmate nodes. Imported .3dm, .obj and IFC enter through a Placement port.
inputs: PVV consumes Floors, Program, Site.area_m2 and a brief id. Today only through its file importer (app.js line 841); unknown ids such as O1 are rejected and repeated levels throw.
Vista consumes Site, Placement, Massing (prism or mesh) and views.ceiling. Today by hand: .3dm and .obj are read as-is and placement is declared by the user.
Form Studio consumes Site (parcel ring or point) and brief constants, from presets, map click or City lookup.
Toolbench shell consumes node manifests; today a hard-coded TOOLS array in index.html.
DT Mass would consume Site and offer Floors; Solar would consume Floors[0], rotation and storeys. Both only with consent.

Vista produces ViewStudy and Checks (plan overlap by view_number, study ceiling).
PVV produces Checks (verdict, FSR) and ledgers under ext.pvv.
DT Mass produces prisms (x, y, w, d, z0, floors, f2f), Floors and rule verdicts (pass, fail, review with clause), in frame legacy-dtmass-1.

DT Mass also carries 6,319 City 2009 footprints with hgt_agl only, while the others use OSM or the studio model. PVV's basemap came from Vista's generator. Rank services by copies x bytes x risk and by how little each tool must change. For 13 Nov only the frame and the cone pack are built; the rest wait.

modules.name: Context packs and storage budget
modules.design_question: How should Layer 0 context data be packaged so every tool loads the same bytes once, with measured geodetic heights, and the repository stays small?
modules.method: A pack is one .bin per layer plus a JSON manifest (layer table of dtype, byte_offset, count; extent; quantum; attribution; caveats), as PVV does, and a release manifest with SHA-256, as Vista does. Buildings: parts per City bldgid, each {ring, base_dm, top_dm, height_source, year, osm_way} in int16 at 0.25 m, heights geodetic with the pack's vertical declared. Primary source: City 2009 LiDAR footprints (124,181 parts with measured top and base); OSM only for buildings absent in 2009, flagged. Estimate: DT Mass's 6,319 downtown parts (46,566 vertices) need about 230 KB, 36.5 B per part. PVV holds 5,247 OSM buildings at 49.8 B each; Vista's mesh 982 B each. Terrain stays a triangle mesh until the terrain packet decides; hand it the 1 m DEM and LiDAR 2022. Host packs in one Pages repo (site 1 GB). Pages sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, ETag and Accept-Ranges (checked 21 Oct), so tiles can be fetched by byte range and cached by SHA-256. Keep ODbL packs in their own folder. Vista's 38.7 MB packs stay out until cleared (M07).

modules.name: Licence and attribution decisions
modules.design_question: Which licence applies to each part of the platform, and which decisions are still open?
modules.method: Start from facts. None of the four repos has a LICENSE file for its own code (PVV's README says to be decided); GitHub says that without a licence no one may reproduce, distribute or derive. List every component by type (code, schema, data packs, images, icons, fonts, vendored libraries) with the licence found in the repo or at source; keep share-alike data in separate folders so it cannot reach code. The OGL-Vancouver text was read on 21 Oct: worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual; copy, modify, publish, distribute for any lawful purpose; attribution 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Vancouver.'; no share-alike. OSM's Licensing Working Group lists Vancouver as approved, so City data may sit in an ODbL pack with both credits; still ask the City in writing. Council documents carry no licence statement: cite and quote briefly. Recommend Apache-2.0 for code (patent grant, NOTICE, change marking; MIT is shorter), CC0 or CC BY 4.0 for the schema, a per-pack licence file for data. Vista's 38.7 MB packs derive from a studio model with unknown owner: mark non-redistributable until cleared. Record each co-author's written agreement before release.

flags.claim: The local frame is accurate because eight OSM footprints match within 0.08 m (Vista data/geo.json).
flags.correction: The check shows the Rhino model was built with the same formula, not agreement with the ground. Scale is 0.58% short N-S and 0.19% short E-W; areas are 0.77% small.
flags.detail: 110,574 m per degree is the equatorial value; 111,215 m applies at 49.28 N. Checks comparing true-metre massing with stored parcel polygons carry about 0.8% area bias. See M03.

flags.claim: The City's view-cone object_id is a stable key (Vista stores object_id 3 for view 10).
flags.correction: The live API returns object_id 1 for view 10. Key cones on view_number plus a polygon hash.
flags.detail: Polygon vertices for view 10 are identical in Vista and the live record, so only the id changed.

flags.claim: PVV's README floor-list example (programme ids O1 and T4) can be imported, and templates/ holds CSV and JSON templates.
flags.correction: O1 and T4 are value-row ids; the importer throws unknown programme. Valid ids come from the catalogue (WK1, SE1, AM4). templates/ holds only .gitkeep; the CSV template is a string at app.js line 859.
flags.detail: Fix the README before publishing any Layer 0 example that copies it.

flags.claim: Four or more distinct rhino3dm builds ship across Vista, Form Studio, Solar and DT Mass.
flags.correction: Three builds: Vista 8.35.0, Form Studio and DT Mass (byte-identical, npm 8.17.0), Solar 8.4.0.
flags.detail: Git blob SHAs of vendor/rhino3dm.wasm (34e610b5) and .min.js (ef4e84ef) equal DT Mass src files; hashing npm tarballs identifies 8.17.0. Shared build is MIT third-party code.

flags.claim: DT Mass works in local metres from the parcel south-west corner, and its view-cone copy is only suspected.
flags.correction: DT Mass has a fixed city frame: origin (-123.118, 49.283), scale [72,616.63, 110,574]; its city-data.js holds 17 view cones, 6,319 City 2009 footprints, 272 zoning polygons, 4,348 parcels.
flags.detail: The origin lies 196.07 m east and 33.17 m north of Vista's. Cone polygons match the City within 0.06 m. Add converter legacy-dtmass-1.

flags.claim: Only view 10's object_id changed (3 in Vista, 1 live).

flags.detail: Checked against the live API on 21 Oct 2026; five ids unchanged (views 21, 28, D, J1, 27.2).

flags.claim: Context building heights must come from OSM tags or estimates (PVV subset 24% measured), with terrain from 60 m SRTM.
flags.correction: Primary sources: City building-footprints-2009 (124,181 LiDAR parts with geodetic top and base, bldgid groups) and LiDAR 2022 (0.081 m vertical) plus the 1 m DEM. OSM only for buildings after 2009; SRTM beyond City coverage.
flags.detail: Footprints are approximate and omit later buildings; datum for footprints not named on the portal. See M06.

flags.claim: Switching to EPSG:3157 brings distance and area error within the 0.05% target.
flags.correction: UTM scale factor near Vancouver is 0.99960087: distances 0.040% short, areas 0.080% short. Use a local TM with k=1 as working frame; keep EPSG:3157 for exchange.
flags.detail: Library Square grid area 11,906.62 m2 against 11,916.13 m2 ellipsoidal. Local TM matches to 0.001 m2.

flags.claim: The Orthophotos_2022 licence is not shown and its terms are unverified.
flags.correction: The open-data dataset orthophoto-imagery-2022 is OGL-Vancouver, EPSG:26910, 7.5 cm, captured 6 June to 1 July 2022. Only the ArcGIS tile endpoint's own terms remain unconfirmed.
flags.detail: Record modified 2024-05-08, 470 tile links. Keep the tile layer off by default.

flags.claim: PVV's floor record can be adopted unchanged with optional tower_id and plan_ref, and a Layer 0 floors array imports into PVV unchanged.
flags.correction: floors[] is unique on (tower_id, level). PVV throws on repeated levels and drops extra keys, so its adapter filters one tower or aggregates, and foreign fields round-trip through the host or ext.pvv.
flags.detail: normaliseFloors, app.js lines 52 to 77. Multi-tower clusters from Form Studio need the two-tower fixture. The zero-change round-trip metric fails without the adapter.

flags.claim: Layer 0 heights can be compared with view-cone ceilings without declaring a vertical datum.
flags.correction: Every height-bearing object carries vertical{datum, grade_z_m, grade_source}; comparisons return unknown unless datums match. City LiDAR is CGVD28 (Metro Vancouver geoid); EGM96 for SRTM; Vista and Form Studio z are model-relative or assumed.
flags.detail: Guidelines set the lower boundary as a maximum geodetic height. The City itself corrected a geodetic grade error of 2.52 m in CD-1 (761). NRCan: CGVD28 and CGVD2013 differ by up to -65 to +55 cm.

flags.claim: Layer 0 lon/lat can be treated as WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) as in GeoJSON.
flags.correction: Portal lon/lat equal NAD83(CSRS) coordinates (parcel corner within 0.11 m of council UTM values); true WGS 84 (ITRF) differs by about 2 m. Layer 0 declares NAD83(CSRS) as served and flags GNSS or WGS 84 inputs.
flags.detail: NRCan puts the two origins about 2 m apart. NATRF2022 will replace NAD83(CSRS) (federal early 2027), changing coordinates by 1 to 2 m.

flags.claim: PVV README: 116 automated tests.
flags.detail: 118 test() calls were counted in 13 files. Node is not installed here, so nothing was run.

flags.claim: NASA SRTM is public domain (PVV README).
flags.detail: The USGS and Open Topo Data pages state no licence or citation request. The USGS page gives EGM96 heights and no accuracy figure. Confirm before shipping terrain.

flags.claim: Hub v0.5 already reads tool exports into one project file (toolbench About page).
flags.detail: No hub code, schema or exports are in the four repos, so its 89/89 checks cannot be verified. A Structure Lab station is named in a caption but no such tool was found. Reconcile with Layer 0.

flags.claim: City open data may be combined with OSM data in one published database.
flags.detail: OGL-Vancouver text read: no share-alike or no-combination clause; OSM's Licensing Working Group lists Vancouver as approved (wiki capture 23 Sep 2026). Written City confirmation still advisable; keep layers in separate files until then.

flags.claim: The supplied studio model and the competition base model may be redistributed in derived form.
flags.detail: Terms unknown for the studio model (owner not recorded); Vista already serves 38.7 MB derived from it. Competition terms cover templates only (7.5.5, 7.5.6). Mark Vista packs non-redistributable until cleared; Form Studio omits the competition model.

flags.claim: Classmates are content to be linked and shown in the toolbench.
flags.detail: Credit lines exist but no consent record is in any repo. The toolbench links to class-toolkit anchors, not to the authors' own pages (xubynii.github.io/dtmass, willemgirard03.github.io/Shading-tool-test).

flags.claim: OSM's tile server can carry the platform's map traffic (Form Studio calls tile.openstreetmap.org).
flags.detail: The policy sets no numeric limit, bans bulk download and prefetching, requires visible attribution and a Referer, and may block heavy use. GitHub Pages is not mentioned. Plan a fallback map.

flags.claim: Public Views Guidelines page and clause numbers quoted in Vista.
flags.detail: Live PDF (amended 4 Feb 2026) returns 403. June 2025 edition read: clauses 3.1.1 to 3.1.5 sit under heading 3.2, cap 2 m in 3.1.5. Feb 2026 text not read; RTS 18292 changes read instead.

flags.claim: The team can license AI-drawn glyphs, pictograms and AI-written code as its own.
flags.detail: Canadian law on AI authorship is unsettled (CIPPIC v Sahni; the article read dates from July 2024 and the outcome was not checked). Disclose AI use in NOTICE and prefer permissive licences.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra is available to the team for adapter work.
flags.detail: Press reports a 3 Sep 2026 launch with staged access; API availability is not stated on the page read. Do not plan around it.

flags.claim: A Form Studio .3dm lands on the right ground in Vista.
flags.detail: Form Studio exports Vista-frame XY with grade z=0; Vista's example site sits at z 40.52 m, model-relative (City LiDAR gives 30.7 to 31.2 m there), and its importer leaves placement to the user. Layer 0 needs Placement and vertical on every massing.

flags.claim: Council 'geodetic height' ceilings are in CGVD28 (Metro Vancouver geoid).
flags.detail: Guidelines and RTS 18292 say geodetic without naming a datum; only City LiDAR names CGVD28GVRD. Stored as inferred. Ask views@vancouver.ca for the cone elevations and datum in writing.

flags.claim: The open-data view-cone polygons match the current Council-approved views.
flags.detail: RTS 18292 (4 Feb 2026) moved the origin of 9.1 and 9.2 to the City Hall stairs; dataset descriptions still name the Walking Figures plaza. View 28 is present, 12.2 absent (still named in Guidelines 3.4.2). Trout Lake changes referred back.

flags.claim: The 59.8 m ceiling of view 27.1 explains the City's statement that 2611 Victoria Dr encroaches 'above the 10th storey'.
flags.detail: Grade 36.2 to 36.8 m (City 2009 LiDAR) gives about 23 m allowed, 7 to 8 storeys at 3.2 m. Datum, plane definition ('measured from' a parcel corner) or storey height may explain the gap; unreconciled.

flags.claim: View 20 (Granville Street) height limit 98.4 m (search summary of a 2026 report for 1188 Cardero St).
flags.detail: Council documents RTS 18621 and others returned 403; the figure came from a search snippet only. Not used in any case or pack until the document is read.

flags.claim: The full integration plan (about 37 to 41 person-days) fits before 13 Nov.
flags.detail: It does not: two people, 17 working days after the 11 Nov holiday, shared with the cone-height and terrain packets. M08 cuts to about 14 to 16 person-days; float 2 to 3 days.
